claim:
The rotary on `11 07` and the rotary on `03 00` are the rotary of `01 22`, above the settings where the rotor being read is still on its way -- which is value 16 on the low rotor and 17 on the high, and not one boundary for both. `01 22` prints ten rotary parameters at `03` through `0B` and then, after an address no page names at `0C`, at `0D`; `11 07` prints the same ten at `08` through `10` and then `11`, with nothing between, so nine of them move five addresses and the tenth moves four. Swept on both and laid over each other, from value 16 to the top of the byte the two are 0.6 cents apart at worst -- across both places the shared table folds, at both take lengths the single type was read at, and at value 32 which was taken at both lengths as the tie. This is the third pair of a multi and its single-effect sibling to be asked and the first read by a stage that recovers a frequency rather than a level, so the agreement is not something a band reading could have manufactured. A third type carries the same ten at `0A` through `12` and then `13` -- nine move seven addresses and the tenth six, a third renumbering and the first read with a drive standing in front of the block rather than a branch beside it. Both of its rotors were swept and laid over the single type's own records: out of transit it stands within 0.74 cents of the single type, and at five of the thirteen settings asked out of transit the two return the same number to four decimal places. The widest any two of the three stand apart is 1.35 cents, between the two multis at value 32 -- the one setting taken at both take lengths, where each type disagrees with itself by as much (1.11 cents on the single type and 1.35 on this one). That is the floor two take lengths put under the comparison and not a distance between the types.

Below value 16 the two disagree by as much as 1507.2 cents, and this says nothing about either block. The same byte at the same value on the same type returns three different rates depending on how many bytes the run wrote before it -- 0.5934 Hz at value 12 after two writes, 0.5472 after three, 0.4042 after thirteen, which is what the multi returns after three and after nineteen. Down there a reading is of the byte and to when the write arrived, and neither record states it.

The high rotor answers the same way and the distance is not one number. The pair's other rotor was read on both types in one run, at one settle, with each type's other rotor silenced, and at the three settings both were asked it returns the same rate to between a tenth and a third of a cent. Its distance short of the printed entry is 0.056 to 0.061 Hz on both, agreeing to between a ten-thousandth and thirteen ten-thousandths of a hertz -- a second quantity the table does not contain, at a second address pair. And it is not an unrelated second quantity: the low rotor's distance over this one is 4.00 at the setting where the shared rate table steps by a twentieth of a hertz, and 4.19 and 4.39 at the two where it steps by a tenth and a half, against the 4.00 the two entries of this unit's own acceleration table give for the two bytes both types rest those rotors at. The drift is ordered the way the table's coarseness is, and the distance is read against that table.
named: one rotary, reached through a renumbering that is not a shift
adds: The records say what each setting of one rate byte modulated at, on two types, at two take lengths, and under five different counts of how many bytes the run wrote first. What is added here is the comparison: which settings the two types agree at, how far apart they are where they do not, and which of two named causes survives being asked.
refutedBy: Either rotor's rate differing between the two types by more than a cent at any setting out of transit -- from value 16 upward on a low rotor and 17 on a high one, under any state both types can be put in.
couldHaveBeenRefutedBy: The run that made it. Ten settings on the multi were laid over the single type's own records at the same settings, at both take lengths those records were read at, with value 32 taken at both as the tie -- and six of the sixteen comparisons came back over a hundred cents apart. That the six are the six where one type disagrees with itself is a second measurement and not a reading of the first.
whatItWouldChange: A renderer holding one rotary and reaching it from both types, rather than one per type. The renumbering is a table of addresses and not a shift, so it has to be read off the pages per type either way.

What a rate byte's reading means near the bottom of its range on any accelerating type. The quantity that moved it here is how long the run took before writing, which no record in this archive states.

alternatives.reading: Two rotaries built to one description, agreeing because they index one printed table, rather than one block reached twice.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The high rotor of the same pair. This reading says the two agree because they index one printed table, and they agree on two quantities the table does not contain: the low rotor's distance short, 0.244 to 0.246 Hz on both, and the high rotor's, 0.056 to 0.061 on both. What refutes the reading is the agreement, which is a difference of two measurements and needs no table: two implementations reading one printed table would agree on the table and there is no reason they would agree on a distance the table does not contain, at two address pairs, to a thousandth of a hertz. Read in data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-rate/01-22-07-silence-the-other-stage-HiSlowalone.json and data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-rate/11-07-0C-silence-the-other-stage-RTHalone.json.

separatedBy.observable: A quantity the printed table does not contain. The table is public and two implementations reading it would agree on it; what they would not agree on is the distance the rotor stops short by, which is this unit's own and is printed nowhere. It holds at 0.244 to 0.246 Hz on both types from value 16 to 127, which is already a quantity outside the table -- but it is one number, and one number is a coincidence a second implementation could reach.

predicts.one block reached twice: The high rotor's own constant, which is a different number on the same type (0.0582 Hz against 0.2425), agrees across the pair as well.
predicts.two implementations of one table: Either constant differing between the types by more than the few thousandths of a hertz each holds to within.

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: A few thousandths of a hertz, which is what each constant holds to across its own type's sweep. The high rotor's constant is a twentieth of the low one's, so it is the harder of the two to reach by accident.

run.why:
The high rotor's slow rate on the multi, against the record of the single type's that this archive already holds. It is the same block, so nothing new has to be held; what is new is that the constant it carries is a different number, and two numbers outside the printed table agreeing is what one number cannot be.

Above value 16 only, and with the low rotor silenced at its level byte the way this pair's low reading silenced the high one. The bottom is not asked: it is not a reading of the byte alone until the write timing is a stated part of the record, which is a change to how a run is recorded and not a run.

alternatives.reading: The bottom of the byte is where the two blocks differ, rather than where neither record is a reading of the byte alone.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The single type returning three different rates at one value of one byte, under three counts of how many bytes were written first, with the type never changing. A difference that one type produces against itself cannot be evidence about two.

alternatives.reading: One rotor routine written once and instantiated twice, rather than one block reached from two types.

separatedBy.why_not_separable: Nothing this archive can measure. Two instances of one routine and one routine reached twice return the same rate, the same distance short and the same ratio between the rotors, and what leaves the sockets is the only thing that can be asked here. This is the residue of the reading above once the coincidence in it is refuted, and it is carried the way the same alternative is carried on the claim about `11 08`'s two halves rather than queued behind a run that could not answer it.
